key_insight: Selenium alloying and air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% maximum efficiency.
engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improving oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers made by vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate TeO2:Se powder mixtures at a 90:10 weight ratio.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours to modify composition and defect chemistry.
Fabricate and evaluate ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag solar cells.
evidence_signal: Optimized 80 nm absorbers annealed for 9 hours yielded 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent response from 300–1000 nm; residual metallic Te was reduced to approximately 0.4%.
watch_item: The 9-hour anneal may constrain manufacturing throughput, while long-term device stability is not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
